```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Obert_2026_fentanyl_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Obert_2026_fentanyl_rat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dmd.2026.100390> (open access,
  PMC13670244). The population PK control stream is Supplemental Material 1
  of the article.

Obert et al. gave Sprague-Dawley rats an overdose-level intravenous fentanyl
bolus (100 ug/kg) twice a week for five weeks and measured fentanyl and
norfentanyl in arterial plasma after the 1st, 5th and 10th injections. They
analysed the data three ways: noncompartmental analysis, a NONMEM population
PK model, and a PK-Sim PBPK model. This article packages the population PK
model. The PBPK model is a platform (PK-Sim) model whose tissue
partitioning, permeability and enzyme-abundance machinery is not published in
a form that can be re-expressed as ODEs, so it is not included.

# Population

The model was fitted to 19 adult Sprague-Dawley rats (9 female, 10 male),
giving data from 7 animals of each sex at every sampled injection (Results,
Study population). At baseline the females were older (13.4 vs 8.9 weeks) and
lighter (286 vs 343 g) than the males; animals weighed 280-380 g on arrival.
Each rat received 100 ug/kg fentanyl as a tail-vein bolus twice weekly with at
least 72 h between injections, for 10 injections. Arterial blood was drawn 3,
15, 30, 60, 180 and 360 min after the 1st, 5th and 10th injections (the 11th
for 4 animals). Weight and age were tested in the stepwise covariate search
and not retained; sex and injection number were retained.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Obert_2026_fentanyl_rat")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value comes from Table 3 of the article (final estimates); the model
structure comes from the NONMEM control stream (Supplemental Material 1) and
the model schematic (Supplemental Figure 1).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CLFent) | log(774 mL/h) | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (VFent,Central) | log(275 mL) | Table 3 |
| `lq` (QFent) | log(232 mL/h) | Table 3 |
| `lvp` (VFent,Peripheral) | log(326 mL) | Table 3 |
| `lkm_norfentanyl` (Km) | log(2.89 ng/mL) | Table 3 |
| `lvmax_norfentanyl` (Vmax) | log(78.8 ng/h) | Table 3 (units: see below) |
| `lcl_norfentanyl` (CLNor) | log(23.6 mL/h) | Table 3 |
| `lvc_norfentanyl` (VNor) | log(10.4 mL) | Table 3 |
| `e_sexf_cl` | -0.158 | Table 3 'CLFent:Sex'; `CLSEX` block of the control stream |
| `e_cycle10_cl` | -0.0796 | Table 3 'CLFent:Injection'; `CLINJ` block |
| `e_sexf_vmax_norfentanyl` | -0.764 | Table 3 'Vmax:Sex'; `VMAXSEX` block |
| `e_sexf_cl_norfentanyl` | -0.445 | Table 3 'CLNor:Sex'; `NCLSEX` block |
| `etalcl` | 0.00843 | Table 3 omega2 CL,Fent |
| `etalvmax_norfentanyl` | 0.0716 | Table 3 omega2 Vmax |
| `etalcl_norfentanyl` | 0.0602 | Table 3 omega2 CL,Nor |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.112) = 0.335 | Table 3 'Prop. error, fentanyl' ($SIGMA variance) |
| `propSd_norfentanyl` | sqrt(0.261) = 0.511 | Table 3 'Prop. error, norfentanyl' ($SIGMA variance) |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | `$DES` DADT(1), DADT(2); Supplemental Figure 1 |
| `d/dt(central_norfentanyl)` | n/a | `$DES` DADT(3) = VMAX*C1/(KM+C1) - NCL/V3*A(3) |
| `Cc_norfentanyl` scaling 232.3/336.5 | n/a | `$PK` S3 = V3*(336.5/232.3) |
| Covariate forms `(1 + theta * indicator)` | n/a | `$PK` CLSEX, CLINJ, VMAXSEX, NCLSEX blocks |

## Notes on the structure

* **Norfentanyl formation does not deplete fentanyl.** In the control stream
  the fentanyl central compartment loses drug only through CLFent and Q; the
  Michaelis-Menten formation term appears only in the norfentanyl equation.
  The packaged model keeps that form. The formation rate never exceeds Vmax
  (78.8 ng/h), against a fentanyl clearance flux of ~77 000 ng/h at the first
  sample, so the omission is numerically negligible.
* **Vmax is an amount rate.** Table 3 prints the unit of Vmax as "ng/mL per
  h", but the control stream adds `VMAX*C1/(KM+C1)` directly to `DADT(3)`,
  whose state `A(3)` is an amount (the code itself computes
  `C3 = A(3)/V3`). Vmax is therefore in ng/h, in fentanyl-mass equivalents
  because the dose is entered as fentanyl ng.
* **Molecular-weight conversion.** The norfentanyl compartment is carried in
  fentanyl-mass equivalents and the control stream reports it through the
  scale `S3 = V3*(336.5/232.3)`, so the modelled norfentanyl concentration is
  `central_norfentanyl / vc_norfentanyl * 232.3 / 336.5` ng/mL.
* **Sex coding.** The control stream applies `(1 + THETA)` when `SEX = 0`.
  The text states that clearance, Vmax and norfentanyl clearance are lower in
  females, so `SEX = 0` is female and the canonical `SEXF = 1 - SEX` carries
  the coefficients unchanged.
* **Injection number** is the canonical dose-number counter `CYCLE`
  (1 = first injection). The model applies the clearance effect when
  `CYCLE >= 10`, reproducing the control stream's dichotomy (injection 10
  versus injections 1 and 5; the 4 animals sampled at the 11th injection are
  treated as the 10th).

# Virtual cohort

The cohort has 100 female and 100 male rats, each receiving the full
10-injection course: injections on a Monday/Thursday schedule (72 h and 96 h
intervals alternating), so the 10th injection falls on day 31 as in the
article. The dose is 100 ug/kg = 1e5 ng per kg of current body weight.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

n_per_sex <- 100
dose_times <- c(0, 72, 168, 240, 336, 408, 504, 576, 672, 744)
sampled_inj <- c(1, 5, 10)
# Nominal sampling times (h): 3, 15, 30, 60, 180, 360 min, plus a dense grid
# for the prediction-interval plot.
# Times are built from whole minutes so that the nominal samples can be
# matched exactly after the solve.
nominal_min <- c(3, 15, 30, 60, 180, 360)
nominal <- nominal_min / 60
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(0, nominal_min, seq(6, 360, by = 6)))) / 60

rats <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_per_sex),
  SEXF = rep(c(1L, 0L), each = n_per_sex),
  sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1L, "Female", "Male"),
  # baseline weight (kg) around the reported sex means (286 g, 343 g)
  wt1 = ifelse(SEXF == 1L, 0.286, 0.343) * exp(rnorm(2 * n_per_sex, 0, 0.06)),
  # weight at the 10th injection, so that the mean over the course equals
  # the PBPK individuals' mean weight over all injection days (Table 1:
  # 328 g female, 374 g male)
  wt10 = wt1 * ifelse(SEXF == 1L, 2 * 0.328 / 0.286 - 1, 2 * 0.374 / 0.343 - 1)
)

doses <- rats |>
  tidyr::crossing(CYCLE = 1:10) |>
  mutate(
    time = dose_times[CYCLE],
    WT = wt1 + (wt10 - wt1) * (CYCLE - 1) / 9,
    amt = 1e5 * WT,
    evid = 1L,
    cmt = "central",
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )

obs <- rats |>
  tidyr::crossing(CYCLE = sampled_inj, tad = obs_grid) |>
  mutate(
    time = dose_times[CYCLE] + tad,
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "central",
    dvid = 1L
  )

events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  mutate(injection = paste("Injection", CYCLE)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, dvid, SEXF, CYCLE, sex, injection)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Obert_2026_fentanyl_rat")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("sex", "injection", "CYCLE"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(CYCLE %in% sampled_inj) |>
  mutate(
    tad_min = round((time - dose_times[CYCLE]) * 60),
    tad = tad_min / 60
  ) |>
  filter(tad_min >= 0, tad_min <= 360)
```

`Cc` and `Cc_norfentanyl` are individual predictions. Where a comparison is to
observed data (means, SDs and percentiles of plasma concentrations), the
proportional residual error is added explicitly with the packaged SDs:

```{r residual}
pars <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
sim <- sim |>
  mutate(
    Cfent_obs = Cc * (1 + pars[["propSd"]] * rnorm(n())),
    Cnor_obs = Cc_norfentanyl * (1 + pars[["propSd_norfentanyl"]] * rnorm(n()))
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: mean (SD) concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
fig1 <- sim |>
  filter(tad %in% nominal) |>
  select(sex, injection, tad, Fentanyl = Cfent_obs, Norfentanyl = Cnor_obs) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Fentanyl, Norfentanyl), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(analyte, sex, injection, tad) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(conc), sd = sd(conc), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(fig1, aes(tad, mean, colour = sex, shape = injection)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.15)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 1e-3), ymax = mean + sd),
    width = 0,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.15)
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = interaction(sex, injection)), alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Female = "firebrick", Male = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after injection (h)",
    y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Obert 2026 (mean and SD at the nominal sampling times)."
  )
```

As in the article, the fentanyl profiles of the two sexes overlap, while
norfentanyl is about 3-fold lower in females. The model has no sex or weight
effect on the fentanyl volumes, so the females' smaller absolute dose gives
them a slightly lower simulated early fentanyl concentration, whereas the
observed female means were slightly higher (see the NCA comparison below).

## Supplemental Figure 2c: visual predictive check

```{r figure-s2c, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(tad > 0) |>
  select(tad, Fentanyl = Cfent_obs, Norfentanyl = Cnor_obs) |>
  pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(analyte, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(conc, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(p05, 1e-3), ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "slateblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after injection (h)",
    y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Simulated 5th-95th percentile band and median; compare Supplemental Figure 2c of Obert 2026."
  )
```

The simulated 5th-95th percentile band spans about 47-170 ng/mL fentanyl at
3 min and 0.17-0.86 ng/mL at 6 h, against observations of about 40-240 and
0.25-0.75 ng/mL in Supplemental Figure 2c. The norfentanyl 95th percentile
(about 3 ng/mL at 1-1.5 h) matches the highest observations. The lower
percentiles are pulled far below the lowest observations because the
proportional residual SD of 0.51 sends the lower tail towards zero, and the
band pools both sexes; the article's own fentanyl VPC shows the same widening
of the simulated lower band at late times.

# Residual-error scale

Table 3 lists the residual errors as 0.112 and 0.261. These are the
`$SIGMA` estimates of `Y = F*(1 + ERR)`, which NONMEM holds as variances, so
the proportional SDs are `sqrt(0.112) = 0.335` and `sqrt(0.261) = 0.511`. The
data confirm the variance reading. The fentanyl volumes carry no IIV, so the
spread of the first (3-min) fentanyl concentration within a sex is almost
entirely residual error: the article's within-sex CV of fentanyl Cmax is
25-35% (Supplemental Table 1), which the SD reading (11%) cannot produce.

```{r residual-check}
cv_cmax <- sim |>
  filter(tad_min == 3) |>
  group_by(sex, injection) |>
  summarise(cv = sd(Cfent_obs) / mean(Cfent_obs), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(
  cv_cmax |> rename(Sex = sex, Injection = injection, "CV of 3-min fentanyl" = cv),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Simulated CV of the 3-min fentanyl concentration (published Cmax CV 25.1-35.1%)."
)

stopifnot(
  # Variance reading gives ~0.33, the SD reading ~0.11 -- a mis-read SIGMA
  # lands far outside this band.
  abs(median(cv_cmax$cv) - 0.33) < 0.08
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The article's noncompartmental analysis (Phoenix WinNonlin, linear trapezoid)
used the six nominal samples per injection. The same sampling is applied to
the individual predictions here, with each injection's 6-h profile analysed
on its own time-after-dose axis. Fentanyl Cmax is taken over the samples
(3 min onwards); the fentanyl time-zero row is the post-bolus concentration
`dose / Vc`, which anchors AUC the way Phoenix's back-extrapolated C0 does.
Norfentanyl peaks at about 1 h, so its terminal half-life is regressed on the
1-, 3- and 6-h samples.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(tad %in% c(0, nominal)) |>
  select(id, sex, injection, tad, Cc, Cc_norfentanyl) |>
  mutate(group = paste(sex, injection, sep = ", "))

nca_dose <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, CYCLE %in% sampled_inj) |>
  transmute(id, sex, injection, tad = 0, amt, group = paste(sex, injection, sep = ", "))

# A profile whose norfentanyl peak falls on the 3-h sample has only two
# points for the terminal regression; its half-life and AUCinf are left
# missing (counted below) rather than reported as a warning per rat.
muffle_too_few_points <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("Too few points for half-life", conditionMessage(w))) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}

run_nca <- function(conc_col, intervals, route) {
  conc <- nca_conc |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    rename(conc = all_of(conc_col))
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ tad | group + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | group + id, route = route)
  withCallingHandlers(
    PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
      conc_obj,
      dose_obj,
      intervals = intervals,
      # Norfentanyl peaks at the 1-h sample, leaving only the 3-h and 6-h
      # samples after it; the article reports a half-life for every group,
      # so the peak sample is allowed into the terminal regression.
      options = list(allow.tmax.in.half.life = TRUE)
    )),
    warning = muffle_too_few_points
  )
}

nca_fent <- run_nca(
  "Cc",
  data.frame(
    start = c(0.05, 0),
    end = c(6, Inf),
    cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
    aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
  ),
  route = "intravascular"
)
nca_nor <- run_nca(
  "Cc_norfentanyl",
  data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE),
  route = "extravascular"
)
n_no_hl <- as.data.frame(nca_nor) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", is.na(PPORRES)) |>
  nrow()
```

In `r n_no_hl` of the 600 simulated norfentanyl profiles the peak falls on
the 3-h sample, too late for a three-point terminal regression; those
profiles are left out of the norfentanyl half-life and AUCinf means.

## Comparison against published NCA

Supplemental Table 1 reports arithmetic means by sex and injection, so the
simulated per-rat values are summarised by their mean before comparison.


```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~group, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "Fentanyl", "Female, Injection 1", 132, 57.7, 1.17,
  "Fentanyl", "Male, Injection 1", 108, 53.5, 1.03,
  "Fentanyl", "Female, Injection 5", 107, 48.0, 1.21,
  "Fentanyl", "Male, Injection 5", 116, 58.4, 1.08,
  "Fentanyl", "Female, Injection 10", 140, 62.3, 1.18,
  "Fentanyl", "Male, Injection 10", 115, 60.7, 1.11,
  "Norfentanyl", "Female, Injection 1", 0.812, 3.48, 2.52,
  "Norfentanyl", "Male, Injection 1", 2.46, 7.90, 1.90,
  "Norfentanyl", "Female, Injection 5", 0.833, 4.21, 2.79,
  "Norfentanyl", "Male, Injection 5", 2.27, 7.95, 2.11,
  "Norfentanyl", "Female, Injection 10", 0.800, 3.62, 2.63,
  "Norfentanyl", "Male, Injection 10", 2.67, 10.6, 2.33
)

# One value per rat and parameter: fentanyl Cmax from the 3-min-onwards
# interval, AUCinf and half-life from the 0-Inf interval. Selecting by
# interval drops the companion parameters PKNCA adds to each interval.
nca_values <- function(res, analyte, cmax_start) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(
      (PPTESTCD == "cmax" & start == cmax_start) |
        (PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life") & is.infinite(end))
    ) |>
    transmute(analyte = analyte, group, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
}
nca_ind <- bind_rows(
  nca_values(nca_fent, "Fentanyl", 0.05),
  nca_values(nca_nor, "Norfentanyl", 0)
)

simulated <- nca_ind |>
  group_by(analyte, group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated |> mutate(group = paste(analyte, group, sep = ": ")) |> select(-analyte),
  reference = published |> mutate(group = paste(analyte, group, sep = ": ")) |> select(-analyte),
  by = "group",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Mean simulated NCA vs Supplemental Table 1 of Obert 2026 (arithmetic means, 7 rats per sex and injection). * marks rows differing by >20%."
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
ratio <- simulated |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cmax, aucinf.obs, half.life), names_to = "param", values_to = "sim") |>
  inner_join(
    published |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cmax, aucinf.obs, half.life), names_to = "param", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("analyte", "group", "param")
  ) |>
  mutate(ratio = sim / pub)

knitr::kable(
  ratio |>
    group_by(analyte, param) |>
    summarise(median_ratio = median(ratio), .groups = "drop") |>
    rename(Analyte = analyte, "NCA parameter" = param, "Median simulated / published" = median_ratio),
  digits = 2
)

med_ratio <- function(a, p) median(ratio$ratio[ratio$analyte == a & ratio$param == p])
# Female / male ratio of the group means, simulated and published
sex_ratio <- ratio |>
  filter(analyte == "Norfentanyl", param %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  mutate(sex = sub(",.*", "", group)) |>
  group_by(param, sex) |>
  summarise(sim = mean(sim), pub = mean(pub), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(param) |>
  summarise(
    sim = sim[sex == "Female"] / sim[sex == "Male"],
    pub = pub[sex == "Female"] / pub[sex == "Male"]
  )
knitr::kable(
  sex_ratio |> rename("NCA parameter" = param, "Female / male, simulated" = sim, "Female / male, published" = pub),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Norfentanyl sex difference."
)

stopifnot(
  # Half-lives follow from the disposition parameters (CL, Vc, Q, Vp; and
  # formation-rate-limited norfentanyl elimination); a mis-transcribed
  # volume or clearance moves them by tens of percent.
  abs(med_ratio("Fentanyl", "half.life") - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(med_ratio("Norfentanyl", "half.life") - 1) < 0.2,
  abs(med_ratio("Fentanyl", "aucinf.obs") - 1) < 0.2,
  # The female / male norfentanyl ratio (published 0.43 for AUC, 0.33 for
  # Cmax) is the paper's headline result and is set by the sex effects on
  # Vmax and CLNor.
  all(abs(sex_ratio$sim - sex_ratio$pub) < 0.1),
  # Norfentanyl AUC runs about 20% under the published NCA (see below);
  # dropping the molecular-weight factor would put it at about 1.2, and
  # inverting it at about 0.4.
  med_ratio("Norfentanyl", "aucinf.obs") > 0.65,
  med_ratio("Norfentanyl", "aucinf.obs") < 1.05
)
```

Fentanyl half-life and AUC, norfentanyl half-life, and the 2- to 3-fold
lower norfentanyl exposure in females all reproduce Supplemental Table 1.
Norfentanyl AUC is about 20% and norfentanyl Cmax about 30% below the
published means in both sexes; see the Assumptions and deviations section.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PBPK model not packaged.** The article's PK-Sim PBPK model relies on the
  platform's tissue-partitioning, permeability and enzyme-abundance
  calculations, which are not published in a form that can be re-expressed
  as ODEs. Only the NONMEM population model is packaged.
* **Body weight and dose.** Weight is not a model covariate, but it sets the
  100 ug/kg dose. Baseline weights are drawn around the reported sex means
  (286 g female, 343 g male) and grow linearly over the course so that the
  mean weight across injections matches the PBPK individuals' mean weights
  (Table 1: 328 g female, 374 g male). Individual weights were not published.
* **Dosing schedule.** The article states twice-weekly injections at least
  72 h apart; a Monday/Thursday pattern (alternating 72-h and 96-h intervals)
  is assumed. With a fentanyl half-life near 1 h and norfentanyl near 2 h,
  nothing carries over between injections, so the exact pattern does not
  affect the results.
* **Fentanyl AUC and Cmax.** The model gives fentanyl AUCinf = dose / CL
  exactly (about 44 ng*h/mL for a 343-g male at the first injection), while
  the noncompartmental AUCs in Supplemental Table 1 are 48-62 ng*h/mL, which
  imply a clearance about 20% below the population estimate of 774 mL/h. The
  simulated NCA on the same six samples recovers part of the gap (median
  simulated / published AUC about 0.9), because the linear trapezoid
  overestimates the area under the steep post-bolus decline. Simulated
  fentanyl Cmax at 3 min agrees for males but is lower than the published
  female means (132-140 ng/mL at injections 1 and 10), which exceed the male
  means despite the females' smaller dose; the model has no sex or weight
  effect on the fentanyl volumes and carries no IIV on them. No parameter was
  adjusted.
* **Norfentanyl exposure about 20-30% under the published NCA.** With the
  control stream's molecular-weight scale (`S3 = V3*(336.5/232.3)`) the
  simulated norfentanyl AUC is about 20% and Cmax about 30% below Supplemental
  Table 1 and Figure 1, similarly in both sexes, so the sex difference is
  reproduced. Leaving the scale out would raise every norfentanyl
  concentration by 336.5/232.3 = 1.45, which brings Cmax into agreement in
  both sexes but puts AUC about 15-25% above the published values, so the
  NCA does not clearly favour either reading. The control stream, which
  states the scale explicitly, is followed as published. The article notes some indication
  of instability in the bootstrap, whose 95% intervals for Vmax (10-148),
  CLNor (4-43 mL/h) and VNor (3-18 mL) are wide.
* **Norfentanyl formation does not deplete fentanyl**, and Vmax is an amount
  rate in fentanyl-mass equivalents, both as in the control stream (see
  Notes on the structure).
* **Final estimates.** Values are the final estimates of Table 3. The
  `$THETA` / `$OMEGA` values in Supplemental Material 1 differ slightly
  (for example CL 785, CLINJ10 -0.0928) and are initial estimates of the
  final run.
